title: A code minted on a 'bonus' campaign redeems TRUE, permanently burns the code seat, and delivers nothing — no consumer can ever match the grant
summary: redeem_promo_code never inspects promotions.kind. For kind='bonus' the promotions_kind_shape CHECK forces fee_bps to NULL, so the grant it writes has fee_bps NULL — and every downstream consumer filters that grant out. consume_promo_grant (final definition, 20260806220000:249-264) requires `p2.kind = 'fee_override'` AND `g.fee_bps is not null`; consume_poster_discount (final definition, 20260806340000:86) requires `p2.kind = 'poster_discount'`; consume_fee_credit (20260806080000:160-205) reads bonus_ledger and never touches promo_grants at all; and bonus_ledger rows are minted ONLY by accrue_referral_bonus (20260806250000:41-107), which reads the `referrals` table and never looks at a grant. The bonus grant is therefore inert by construction. The code seat is consumed anyway (line 305-307, default promo_codes.max_redemptions = 1) and the unique index promo_grants_one_per_user_promo (line 128) makes the dead claim permanent — the user can never re-claim that campaign. The admin console actively invites this: <MintCodes id={p.id} /> is rendered for EVERY promotion row with no kind gate (admin/app/(console)/promotions/page.tsx:141) and mintCodes() accepts any promotionId (admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts:111-134).
trigger: Admin creates a 'bonus' campaign ($10 per referral), clicks Mint on its row (the UI offers it), and distributes 200 codes. Any authenticated user calls redeem_promo_code('<code>').
money_impact: Every redeemer is told TRUE (the only signal the RPC produces) and receives exactly $0.00. With the console's mintCodes defaults (200 codes x 1 seat), 200 users get a confirmed-but-empty benefit and 200 codes are permanently spent. The campaign's spent_cents stays 0, so the burn-down bar on /promotions reads 'nothing spent' while the operator believes the offer landed — the loss is trust and support volume, not margin, but it is invisible to every existing control: ctl_benefit_never_settled (20260806220000:295) keys on promo_redemptions, and this path never inserts one.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:305-317 — `update public.promo_codes set redemptions_used = redemptions_used + 1 where id = c.id and redemptions_used < max_redemptions;` ... `insert into public.promo_grants (user_id, promotion_id, code_id, fee_bps, uses_allowed, expires_at) values (uid, p.id, c.id, p.fee_bps, p.uses_allowed, p.ends_at)`. No `p.kind` test anywhere in the function. supabase/migrations/20260806110000_poster_discounts.sql:45 — `(kind = 'bonus' and bonus_cents is not null and fee_bps is null)`. supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:256,264 — `and p2.kind = 'fee_override'` / `if not found or g.fee_bps is null then return null; end if;`. admin/app/(console)/promotions/page.tsx:141 — `<MintCodes id={p.id} />` inside the unconditional promos.map row.
fix_sketch: Reject non-deliverable kinds at the redemption entry point rather than silently succeeding: after loading `p`, `if p.kind not in ('fee_override','poster_discount') then insert attempt(false); return false; end if;` — before the seat increment, so the code is not burned. Independently, gate MintCodes in the console on `p.kind !== 'bonus'` (a bonus campaign has no redeemable string by design; it accrues from the referrals table), and add a control for grants whose (kind, fee_bps) shape no consumer can match.
verifier_note: Severity is high only in the abstract; the harm scenario cannot occur today. (1) NO USER CAN REACH THE RPC. There is no `.rpc("redeem_promo_code")` anywhere in src/, web/, or supabase/functions/ — I enumerated every client RPC call. The only code a user ever types in the product is the signup referral code (AuthScreen.js:300-306 -> signUp -> user_metadata.referral_code -> OnboardingScreen.js:194 recordReferral -> `referrals` table), a completely different mechanism. So '200 users get a confirmed-but-empty benefit and 200 codes are permanently spent' cannot happen — the codes are unredeemable for a reason that has nothing to do with kind. (2) NOTHING IS CHARGED. redeem_promo_code never touches promotions.spent_cents or redemptions_used; only the consume_* functions do. So this is not a 'charged but not delivered' defect and the burn-down bar reading zero is accurate, not misleading. (3) THE 'PERMANENT' HARM IS NULL. The unique index does make the dead claim permanent, but re-claiming a bonus campaign would yield an equally worthless grant — a bonus is delivered from bonus_ledger via the referrals trigger, never from a grant. Nothing is lost. (4) THE MORE INTERESTING VERSION IS ON THE WIRED PATH, and the finding misses it: grant_promotion_to_users (20260806120000:178-205, only definition) has the SAME missing kind gate and IS wired — pricing/PricingControls.tsx:107 -> grantToUsers -> that RPC. An admin picking a bonus campaign in the 'grant to these emails' box mints the identical inert grant, silently, with an audit row saying it succeeded and a success toast counting the grants. That is the reachable instance of this class. Real severity: a latent input-validation gap in a code path with no live callers, plus one reachable-but-harmless variant. Low.

title: The promo-code rate limiter is read-then-decide — the exact anti-pattern the same file forbids for budgets — and is bypassed by concurrency
summary: The 8-attempts-per-hour limit is a `select count(*)` followed by an `if`, with no FOR UPDATE, no advisory lock, no unique index and no conditional-UPDATE. PostgREST runs each RPC in its own READ COMMITTED transaction, so N concurrent invocations all observe the same pre-burst count and all pass the check; the attempt rows they write are invisible to each other until commit. This is precisely the discipline the migration's own header demands elsewhere — 'consume_promo_grant() makes THE INCREMENT BE THE CHECK — a single UPDATE ... WHERE spent < budget with get diagnostics, never read-then-decide' (lines 31-35) — and consume_promo_grant at line 385-390 does exactly that. The limiter, the one control facing an attacker, does not.
trigger: One authenticated account fires C parallel POSTs to /rest/v1/rpc/redeem_promo_code, each with a different candidate code. All C read tries=0 and all C proceed to a full lookup. After the burst commits, subsequent calls see tries=C>=8 and are refused until the rows age out of the 1-hour window.
money_impact: Per-account attempt throughput becomes the attacker's achievable concurrency per hour instead of the advertised 8. No money is lost today because console-minted codes carry 32^8 ~ 1.1e12 entropy (8 chars over a 32-symbol alphabet, admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts:16-22, uniform since 256 mod 32 == 0). The exposure is that the entropy is the ONLY real defence: promo_codes.code permits `length(btrim(code)) between 6 and 32` (line 97) and carries a free-text `source` column for non-console mints, so a single hand-inserted vanity code (e.g. a 6-char campus code, 32^6 ~ 1.07e9) is defended by a limiter whose stated bound is false. A grant on a 0%-fee campaign with uses_allowed up to 20 is worth up to 20 x max_benefit_cents (default $150) = $3,000 of waived fee per stolen code.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:267-273 — `-- Count ATTEMPTS in the window, not successes. 8/hour.` / `select count(*) into tries from public.promo_redeem_attempts where user_id = uid and created_at > now() - interval '1 hour';` / `if tries >= 8 then insert into public.promo_redeem_attempts (user_id, ok) values (uid, false); return false; end if;`
fix_sketch: Make the increment the check, as the budget path already does: insert the attempt row FIRST, then `select count(*)` in the same transaction (the row is now visible to itself) and return false if it exceeds 8 — or serialize on `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('promo_redeem', uid))` before counting. Additionally key a second bucket on something the attacker cannot mint for free (source IP via `current_setting('request.headers')`, or a global per-code failure counter), since today a fresh account resets the entire budget.
verifier_note: Three corrections, all reducing this to low. (1) THE BYPASS IS SMALLER THAN CLAIMED AND SELF-LIMITING. Every refusal also inserts an attempt row, so once a burst of C lands the rolling one-hour count never falls back below 8 while the attacker keeps calling — they get one burst of C, then a full hour of silence before another. Throughput is ~C/hour, not 'unbounded', where C is capped by the Supabase pooler. Call it a 10-50x amplification of an 8/hour limit. (2) THE VANITY-CODE EXPOSURE DOES NOT EXIST. promo_codes carries `revoke all ... from anon, authenticated` and `grant all ... to service_role` (20260806070000:196-201) with no INSERT policy, so the only writer is the console's mintCodes, which mints exactly 8 chars over a 32-symbol alphabet. A 6-char hand-inserted campus code requires an admin writing raw SQL against production — not a user-reachable state, and if that is the threat model the limiter was never the control. Against 32^8 = 1.1e12, even 100 attempts/hour is ~1.2e9 account-hours. (3) THE $3,000 FIGURE IS AN ARITHMETIC CEILING, NOT A WINDFALL. uses_allowed(20) x max_benefit_cents($150) = $3,000 requires twenty separate bookings each generating >=$150 of platform fee. At the standing 1000 bps that is a $1,500 gig each, i.e. ~$30,000 of GMV that the thief must actually WORK — the fee comes out of the earner's payout, so the benefit only materialises as work is delivered and Stripe processing is paid on every cent of it. And consume_promo_grant charges the campaign the worst case at booking against budget_cents (default $25,000) with the increment as the check, so the campaign, not the code, is the binding ceiling. There is no path here to money. Finally, the table this limiter protects will stay permanently empty: redeem_promo_code has zero product callers.

title: redeem_promo_code has zero callers in the product — every code the console mints is undeliverable, and the burn-down UI reports it as 'unused' rather than 'unreachable'
summary: There is no promo-code entry point anywhere in the mobile app, the web app, or the edge functions: `grep -rn "redeem_promo_code"` over src/, web/ and supabase/functions/ returns nothing, and no screen has a code input (the only 'enter your code' UIs are StudentVerifyModal.js:41 and web/app/(app)/verify-student/page.tsx:43, both the .edu email flow). The RPC is granted to `authenticated` and works, but only for someone hand-crafting a PostgREST call. The single wired delivery path is grantToUsers -> grant_promotion_to_users (admin/app/(console)/pricing/actions.ts:122), which is by-email and has no code involved. Meanwhile the Promotions page renders a Codes column with a per-code `redemptions_used/max_redemptions` counter and a Mint button on every campaign.
trigger: Admin mints 200 codes for a campus drop, activates the campaign, distributes the codes on flyers. Every code shows 0/1 on /promotions indefinitely.
money_impact: No margin is lost; the failure is diagnostic. The operator reads '0/1 used' as 'the offer did not land' and draws a false conclusion about demand — the standard response is to widen the discount or extend the run (both of which spend more margin) rather than to wire the redemption screen. Meanwhile every user handed a code experiences a promise the product cannot honour. This also means finding #1 above (bonus-kind codes) is currently latent rather than live: it becomes live the moment a code-entry screen ships.
evidence: admin/app/(console)/promotions/page.tsx:133-141 renders `{c.code} {c.redemptions_used}/{c.max_redemptions}` and `` for every campaign. supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:334 — `grant execute on function public.redeem_promo_code(text) to authenticated, service_role;`. No `.rpc('redeem_promo_code')` exists in src/, web/ or supabase/functions/ (the complete list of client RPCs is my_profile, recompute_user_rating, profile_availability, area_market_stats, create_gig_share, raise_gig_emergency, fee_bps_at, view_gig_share).
fix_sketch: Either ship the code-entry screen (a field on ProfileScreen or in onboarding calling supabase.rpc('redeem_promo_code', { p_code })), or — until then — hide MintCodes and the Codes column behind a feature flag and label the promotions page so an operator cannot mint a code the product cannot accept.
verifier_note: Severity down from medium to low: no margin moves and no user is charged anything, so this is an operability defect rather than a money or authorization one. Two refinements. First, the misreading risk is narrower than stated — the operator's likely inference from '0/1 used' is 'nobody redeemed', and widening a discount that nobody can redeem still spends nothing, because spent_cents only moves inside consume_*. The cost is the flyer print run and the support volume from users holding a code with nowhere to type it. Second, this finding is the correct root cause for #1, #3 and #4, all of which described downstream symptoms of the same missing screen as if they were independent defects; fixing the entry point makes #1 and #3 live and worth fixing first, which is the right sequencing note for whoever ships it.

title: The catch-all exception handler rolls the attempt row back with everything else, so any exception is a free unlogged attempt
summary: `exception when others then return false;` is attached to the function's outermost BEGIN block. In PL/pgSQL that block is an implicit subtransaction: catching an exception rolls back EVERY statement executed inside it, including the `insert into public.promo_redeem_attempts`. So the design claim that an attempt is recorded on every path is false by construction for any path that raises — the caller gets their false, and the limiter's counter never moves. The common invalid-code path returns normally at line 285-286, so this is not a large hole today, but it is a hole that widens with any future constraint: the `on conflict (user_id, promotion_id) do nothing` on line 316 absorbs only that one index, so a FK violation on code_id (the reference is `on delete set null`, so a code deleted concurrently with a claim can race), or any new CHECK on promo_grants, lands in the handler and erases the attempt.
trigger: Any exception inside the function body. Concretely reachable today: statement_timeout or a lock-wait timeout on `update public.promo_codes ... where id = c.id` when many callers contend for one hot code row (the concurrency bypass above makes that contention easy to create), which raises, is swallowed by `when others`, and leaves no attempt row — the attacker retries at no cost to their budget.
money_impact: No direct loss. It removes the only accounting the limiter has, on exactly the paths an attacker generating load is most likely to hit, and it silently discards the diagnostic (`sqlerrm` is never raised as a warning, unlike the pin trigger's `raise warning` at 20260806110000:185) — so a redemption that is failing for an operational reason is indistinguishable from a wrong code both to the user and to the operator.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:327-330 — `exception when others then` / `-- Never leak internals to a caller probing codes.` / `return false;` — with all seven `insert into public.promo_redeem_attempts` statements (lines 271, 276, 285, 292, 300, 309, 325) inside that same block.
fix_sketch: Write the attempt row in a nested block whose failure cannot be undone by the outer handler, or better: log the attempt FIRST (before any work), then do the lookup — the row is then already committed-in-transaction and only a full transaction abort can lose it, which also loses the attacker's request. Add `raise warning 'redeem_promo_code failed: %', sqlerrm;` inside the handler so an operational failure is visible in logs without leaking anything to the caller.
verifier_note: The cited concrete trigger is wrong and the impact needs two qualifications. (1) LOCK CONTENTION ON A HOT CODE ROW IS NOT REACHABLE — it needs many concurrent redemptions of the SAME code, and redeem_promo_code has zero product callers, so there is no traffic to contend. The one exception path I could actually construct is an auth.uid() with no `profiles` row: promo_grants.user_id is FK'd to profiles, so that insert raises — but reaching it requires already holding a valid, active, unexpired code that passed every earlier check, so it yields no brute-force amplification whatsoever. Nothing an attacker controls forces a raise on the cheap invalid-code path, which returns normally at 285-286. (2) THE ROLLBACK IS LOAD-BEARING IN THE SAFE DIRECTION, which the finding does not credit: it also unwinds the `update promo_codes set redemptions_used = redemptions_used + 1` at 305-307, so an exception can never burn a code seat or leave a half-written grant. The function is atomic; the only casualty is one line of limiter accounting on a path that has never executed. What is actually worth doing is the second half of the fix sketch — `raise warning 'redeem_promo_code failed: %', sqlerrm` inside the handler, matching accrue_referral_bonus (20260806250000:100-103), which does exactly that so an operational failure is distinguishable from a wrong code in the logs. Severity stays low, but as a logging-fidelity note rather than an exploitable gap.

title: max_benefit_cents caps the CHARGE but never the DISCOUNT — budget_cents does not bound the platform's real loss
summary: consume_promo_grant clamps the amount it debits from promotions.spent_cents to max_benefit_cents, but the benefit actually delivered is a RATE (bookings.fee_bps_quoted) with no absolute cap anywhere downstream. Whenever a single booking's real fee reduction exceeds max_benefit_cents (default 15000c, and the admin console never exposes the field so every campaign has that default), the campaign's ledger understates the give-away and budget_cents stops being a loss ceiling. settle_booking_benefits re-applies the same clamp at capture, so the understatement is permanent.
trigger: An 'active' fee_override promotion with fee_bps = 0 (the documented '0% on your first gigs' case) and the default max_benefit_cents = 15000. An earner holding a grant books a high-value gig. jobs.pay is server-capped at $10,000 (20260730120000) and hourly gigs multiply pay x estimated_hours, so amount_cents_quoted of 1,000,000c is reachable without any abuse — it is a legal listing.
money_impact:
At amount = 1,000,000c: platform_fee_cents(1000000,1000) = (1000000*1000+5000)/10000 = 100000c; platform_fee_cents(1000000,0) = the Stripe floor ceil(1000000*0.029)+30+25 = 29055c. promo_benefit_cents = 70945c ($709.45) — that is what the platform actually forgoes, because stripe-create-payment-intent sets application_fee_amount from fee_bps_quoted alone (index.ts:206 -> platform_fee_after_credit) with no max_benefit clamp. hit = least(15000, 70945) = 15000c, so the campaign is debited $150 for $709.45 given away — a 79% understatement.

Scaled: a campaign with budget_cents = 500000 ($5,000) permits floor(500000/15000) = 33 redemptions (34 would need 510000 > 500000). Real loss = 33 x 70945c = 2,341,185c = $23,411.85 against a declared $5,000 budget — 4.7x. With the console's default budget of $250 (25000c) a single redemption on a $10,000 gig costs $709.45, i.e. 2.8x the entire campaign budget, and the campaign then correctly reports itself as barely started.

No control catches it: ctl_redemption_double_charge only compares redemptions_used to the row count (both stay consistent), ctl_benefit_never_settled only looks for unsettled rows, and ctl_discount_charged_not_delivered filters p.kind = 'poster_discount'. Nothing compares reserved_cents/benefit_cents to the fee actually foregone. The admin console's own comment (admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts:12) states 'the budget field is the only thing standing between a typo and an uncapped giveaway' — which is precisely the property that does not hold.
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:269
  hit := least(p.max_benefit_cents, public.promo_benefit_cents(p_amount_cents, g.fee_bps));
...:274-276
  update public.promotions
     set redemptions_used = redemptions_used + 1,
         spent_cents      = spent_cents + hit
   where id = p.id and redemptions_used < max_redemptions and spent_cents + hit <= budget_cents;

supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:178-181 (settle re-clamps, permanently)
    actual := least(
      coalesce((select max_benefit_cents from public.promotions where id = r.promotion_id), r.reserved_cents),
      public.promo_benefit_cents(p_amount_cents, r.fee_bps));

supabase/migrations/20260806320000_discount_headroom_after_credit.sql:180-183 (the delivered benefit is a bare rate)
      promoBps := public.consume_promo_grant(new.earner_id, new.id, new.amount_cents_quoted);
      if promoBps is not null then
        new.fee_bps_quoted := least(new.fee_bps_quoted, promoBps);

supabase/functions/stripe-create-payment-intent/index.ts:206  const feeBps = safeBps(booking.fee_bps_quoted);   -- no max_benefit clamp on the money

supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:71-72  max_benefit_cents integer not null default 15000  -- 'Per-booking cap on how much benefit a single use may consume.'

admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts:55-66  -- the insert row sets fee_bps/budget_cents/max_redemptions and NEVER max_benefit_cents; editPromotion (lines 145-192) cannot change it either.
fix_sketch: Either (1) make the cap real by converting it into a floor on the pinned fee: after `least(new.fee_bps_quoted, promoBps)`, clamp so that platform_fee_cents(amount, pre) - platform_fee_cents(amount, post) <= max_benefit_cents, raising fee_bps_quoted back up if it would exceed — the campaign then delivers exactly what it is charged; or (2) drop the clamp from `hit`/`actual` so spent_cents records the true cost and budget_cents genuinely bounds the loss (campaigns will exhaust sooner, which is the honest behaviour). Do not leave the two halves disagreeing. Add a control that recomputes the true foregone fee per redemption and flags reserved/benefit_cents < true cost, and expose max_benefit_cents in /promotions.
verifier_note:
Two corrections to scope, not to mechanism.

(a) The invariant only breaks above a threshold, which the finding does not state. The break needs true benefit > max_benefit_cents = 15000c. At the standing 1000 bps with a 0-bps grant: 0.1a - (0.029a + 55) > 15000 → a > 212,042c ≈ $2,120. Below that, hit is exact and budget_cents bounds the give-away correctly. So this is a large-gig defect, not an every-booking one — which is why 'critical' is overstated. On the marketplace's typical $50–$300 gigs the ledger is accurate.

(b) The platform never pays out of pocket. platform_fee_cents floors at ceil(0.029a)+30+25 unconditionally, so at 0 bps on $10,000 the platform still collects 29055c and covers Stripe. The exposure is forgone margin, not cash loss. The real hard bound is max_redemptions × per-booking-benefit (100 × 70945c ≈ $70,945 for a default campaign), which is a bound in the useless sense — so the finding's core claim ('budget_cents is not a loss ceiling') stands.

The scaled numbers check out as stated: 33 redemptions at 15000c = 495000 ≤ 500000 budget, 34 would be 510000 > 500000; 33 × 70945c = $23,411.85 vs a declared $5,000. And the default $250 budget admits exactly one 15000c redemption, so a single $10,000 booking forgoes $709.45 against a $250 campaign.

Of the two fixes proposed, only (1) — clamping fee_bps_quoted back up so delivered ≤ max_benefit_cents — actually restores the invariant; (2) alone would fix the ledger but still let one booking exceed the whole budget in a single redemption, because the budget check is `spent + hit <= budget` evaluated after the rate was already chosen.

title: A referral bonus is never clawed back once it vests — a refund, chargeback or dispute on day 8 leaves it fully payable
summary: vest_bonuses() is the ONLY writer that can void a bonus, and its void pass is scoped `where b.state = 'pending'`. Once the 7-day timer flips a row to 'payable' (and later 'applied'), no code path in the repository can ever reverse it. The stated guarantee — "payable only after a refund window closes with no reversal" — is therefore only true for reversals that land inside the 7 days.
trigger: A refers B. B's gig is verified on day 0; accrue_referral_bonus mints a pending bonus with vests_at = day 7. The hourly sweep on day 7 flips it to 'payable'. On day 8 the poster charges back, or support issues a refund via the console (record_refund writes payments.refunded_cents), or the poster opens a dispute. vest_bonuses runs again: its void pass matches only state='pending', so the payable row is untouched. A then spends the credit against a future gig's platform fee.
money_impact: The platform pays out the full bonus_cents for a referral whose underlying work was reversed. Stripe's chargeback window is up to 120 days and the console can refund at any time, so the 7-day vest window covers a small fraction of the real reversal window. This is also the deliberate-abuse rail: the pair mints the bonus, waits 8 days, then reverses the source booking and keeps the bonus. Exposure per event = bonus_cents (admin console caps at $500/promotion, DB CHECK caps at 50000c); aggregate exposure = promotions.budget_cents. There is no operator remedy either: admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts revokeGrant only updates promo_grants.revoked_at — grep shows NO admin path that writes bonus_ledger at all, so support cannot cancel a fraudulent credit.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:133-141 — `update public.bonus_ledger b set state = 'void', void_reason = '...' where b.state = 'pending' and exists (select 1 from public.payments p where p.booking_id = b.source_booking_id and (coalesce(p.refunded_cents,0) > 0 or p.status = 'refunded'));`  A repo-wide grep for `bonus_ledger` returns writers in exactly three places: accrue_referral_bonus (insert/delete), vest_bonuses (the two statements above), consume_fee_credit + release_booking_benefits (state applied<->payable). Nothing else sets 'void'. admin/app/(console)/promotions/page.tsx:35 only `.from("bonus_ledger").select("state, amount_cents")` — read-only.
fix_sketch: Add a third statement to vest_bonuses that voids/reverses already-vested rows: `update bonus_ledger set state='void', void_reason='post-vest reversal' where state in ('payable') and exists (refund/dispute on source_booking_id)`, and for state='applied' either debit the user a replacement negative ledger row or block it at claim. Widen the reversal window to match Stripe's chargeback window rather than 7 days, or keep 7 days for payability but keep the reversal check live for 120 days. Add an admin `revokeBonus` action with an audit row.
verifier_note: Downgraded high -> medium on magnitude, not mechanism. Three bounds the finding does not price in. (1) The delivery vehicle caps the loss: a fee credit is only ever redeemable against platform margin (consume_fee_credit's headroom = fee minus the Stripe floor, 20260806080000:176-178), so exposure per event is bonus_cents of margin, not cash off the balance. (2) Aggregate is hard-capped by promotions.budget_cents, enforced as the increment-is-the-check UPDATE at 20260806250000:86-91, and the console caps a bonus at $500 with a $250 default budget. (3) The 'wait 8 days then reverse' abuse rail is weaker than stated: the two reversal channels are an admin console refund (record_refund, 20260804020000:110, service_role-only) which the attacker cannot trigger, or a card chargeback — and a chargeback costs the farmer far more than bonus_cents and costs the platform the whole gig value anyway, so the unclawed bonus is a second-order loss on top of a first-order one. What genuinely deserves attention is the operator gap: support/trust/finance/admin all have literally no lever to cancel a fraudulent or reversed credit, because bonus_ledger has no admin writer at all.

title: Voiding a bonus never returns its campaign budget, and the void simultaneously re-opens the same referrer/referred pair to be charged again
summary: vest_bonuses sets state='void' but never decrements promotions.spent_cents / redemptions_used. release_booking_benefits — the only function that gives budget back — walks promo_redemptions only and knows nothing about bonus_ledger. Worse, bonus_ledger_one_per_referral is a PARTIAL index predicated on `state <> 'void'`, so voiding a bonus drops the pair out of the uniqueness guard and the next gig by the same pair mints and charges a second bonus.
trigger: (a) Ordinary case: A refers B, B's gig verifies, campaign charged bonus_cents. Before day 7 the booking is refunded. vest_bonuses voids the row. promotions.spent_cents stays incremented forever — the campaign has paid for a benefit no user ever received, and legitimate referrers later hit `spent_cents + bonus_cents <= budget_cents` and get nothing. (b) Deliberate: the pair repeats the $10 gig -> verify -> get it refunded loop. Each iteration mints a bonus (the voided row no longer occupies the partial index because of the `state <> 'void'` predicate, and bonus_ledger_dedupe is keyed on source_booking_id which is a NEW booking each time), charges bonus_cents, then voids. Nothing is ever delivered and the whole budget is burned.
money_impact: Direct: campaign budget is consumed for undelivered benefits. On the console defaults (budget $250, max_redemptions 100, bonus $10 = 25 fundable bonuses) five refunded referrals silently destroy $50 of the campaign and deny five real referrers their reward. In the deliberate case the attacker can burn the entire $250 at near-zero cost: the only cash they lose per cycle is the $1.00 platform fee on a minimum $10 gig, and a full refund returns even that (the platform, not the pair, eats the ~$0.59 of Stripe processing). No control detects it: ctl_benefit_never_settled (20260806220000:295-316) joins promo_redemptions only; ctl_bonus_vesting_stalled looks at state='pending'; ctl_referral_bonus_repeat filters `state <> 'void'` so it cannot see repeat charges for the same pair once the earlier rows are void. There is no control anywhere reconciling promotions.spent_cents for kind='bonus' against sum(bonus_ledger.amount_cents).
evidence: Void with no budget reversal — 20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:133-141 (updates bonus_ledger only; no `update public.promotions`). The only budget-returning code — 20260806260000_release_fee_credits.sql:61-62 `update public.promotions set redemptions_used = greatest(0, redemptions_used - 1), spent_cents = greatest(0, spent_cents - r.reserved_cents)` — sits inside `for r in select * from public.promo_redemptions where booking_id = p_booking` (line 55), and a referral bonus never creates a promo_redemptions row. The re-open — 20260806250000_referral_once_per_person.sql:37-39 `create unique index ... bonus_ledger_one_per_referral on public.bonus_ledger (user_id, source_user_id) where reason = 'referral' and source_user_id is not null and state <> 'void';` The charge — same file :86-91.
fix_sketch: In vest_bonuses' void pass, decrement the funding campaign in the same statement family: `update promotions p set spent_cents = greatest(0, spent_cents - v.amount_cents), redemptions_used = greatest(0, redemptions_used - 1) from (voided rows) v where p.id = v.promotion_id`. Drop `and state <> 'void'` from bonus_ledger_one_per_referral so a pair that has already been bonused (and reversed) cannot be charged again; if a second chance is intended, gate it on an explicit `retry_allowed` column rather than on the void state. Add a control asserting `promotions.spent_cents = sum(bonus_ledger.amount_cents where state <> 'void')` for kind='bonus'.
verifier_note: The ordinary case (a) is real and is exactly category-2 'charged but never delivered' — keep it. The deliberate case (b) is mechanically real but is NOT the near-zero-cost self-service budget burn described, and the severity drops to medium because of it. The attacker cannot produce the void state on demand: the void predicate needs payments.refunded_cents > 0, whose only writer is record_refund (20260804020000:110), granted to service_role only and reachable solely through the admin console's refund/record-reversal actions. A card chargeback does NOT set refunded_cents (stripe-webhook recordReversal, index.ts:50-95, inserts a disputes row and nothing else) — so a chargeback does not void the bonus at all, it merely blocks the vest pass while the dispute is open. So the '$250 burned at near-zero cost' loop requires an operator to hand-issue 25 audited refunds. The claim '$1.00 lost per cycle, and a full refund returns even that' is also incomplete: a refund does not return Stripe's ~59c of processing, so each cycle costs the platform real cash on top of the budget leak. Accurate framing: an ordinary, legitimate refund inside the 7-day window permanently overstates a campaign's spend and silently denies a real referrer their reward, and the same pair can then be charged a second time — bounded by budget_cents, not exploitable on demand.

title: The promotions_enabled incident kill switch does not reach referral bonuses at all — neither minting nor spending honours it
summary: app_flags.promotions_enabled is documented as "Master switch for ALL promotions. OFF = no code redeems and no grant applies to a NEW booking" and as the incident switch that turns "everything off at once". consume_promo_grant and consume_poster_discount both read it and early-return. accrue_referral_bonus and consume_fee_credit never read it. Turning it off stops fee overrides and poster discounts while referral bonuses keep minting, keep charging the campaign budget, and keep being spent against platform fees.
trigger: An operator discovers a promotion is being abused at 2am and flips app_flags.promotions_enabled = false, believing all incentive spend has stopped. Every subsequent booking that reaches 'verified' with a referred earner still fires accrue_referral_bonus, which selects an active kind='bonus' promotion with no flag check (line 62-66) and charges spent_cents (line 86-91). Every subsequent booking INSERT still calls consume_fee_credit from pin_booking_amount, which selects payable credits with no flag check and no promotion-status check, reducing the fee the platform collects.
money_impact: The one lever the runbook offers for stopping incentive bleed during an incident leaves the referral rail fully live. Ongoing loss continues at bonus_cents per verified referred gig plus the full face value of every credit spent, bounded only by promotions.budget_cents and the stock of already-vested credits — the latter has no bound at all because bonus_ledger has no expires_at column and consume_fee_credit never consults promotions.status or ends_at, so credits minted by a paused/ended/expired campaign remain spendable indefinitely.
evidence: No flag check when minting — 20260806250000_referral_once_per_person.sql:62-66 `select * into promo from public.promotions where kind = 'bonus' and status = 'active' and starts_at <= now() and (ends_at is null or ends_at > now()) order by created_at desc limit 1;`  No flag check and no promotion join when spending — 20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:181-185 `for r in select id, amount_cents from public.bonus_ledger where user_id = p_user and state = 'payable' and delivery = 'credit' order by created_at asc for update`.  Contrast the sibling functions: 20260806170000_editable_incentives.sql:59-61 `if not coalesce((select enabled from public.app_flags where key = 'promotions_enabled'), true) then return null; end if;` and 20260806320000_discount_headroom_after_credit.sql (consume_poster_discount) which carries the identical guard.
fix_sketch: Add the same three-line guard at the top of accrue_referral_bonus and consume_fee_credit. For consume_fee_credit, decide explicitly whether an already-earned credit should survive its campaign ending (probably yes, it was earned) but must still die under the incident switch (yes) — those are different questions and the code currently answers neither.
verifier_note: One correction that sharpens rather than weakens it. Minting IS stoppable by another lever: accrue_referral_bonus requires promotions.status='active' (20260806250000:63), so setting the bonus campaign to paused/ended halts new bonuses immediately. The genuinely unreachable half is SPENDING — consume_fee_credit consults no flag, no campaign status, no expiry and no revocation, so there is no lever anywhere in the system that stops an already-vested credit from being applied. That is the finding worth acting on; 'referral bonuses keep minting' overstates the incident exposure because the operator has a working per-campaign switch for that half.

title: bonus_cash_payout_enabled is a kill switch no code reads, and a bonus_delivery='cash' promotion is charged to the budget but can never be delivered
summary: A repo-wide grep for `bonus_cash_payout_enabled` returns exactly two hits: the app_flags INSERT that creates it and a comment in the referral migration. No SQL function, edge function, admin action or client reads it. The thing actually preventing cash payout is the `delivery = 'credit'` filter inside consume_fee_credit. Consequently a promotion created with bonus_delivery='cash' mints bonus_ledger rows, charges promotions.spent_cents, vests them to 'payable' — and no code path can ever deliver them.
trigger: Any writer that sets promotions.bonus_delivery = 'cash' (the column defaults to 'credit' and the console never sets it, but the value is legal per the CHECK constraint, and a clonePromotion of such a row or a direct service-role/SQL-editor insert produces one). Every subsequent referral mints `values (referrer, promo.id, 'referral', promo.bonus_cents, promo.bonus_delivery, 'pending', ...)` — delivery='cash'. accrue_referral_bonus charges the campaign. vest_bonuses flips it to 'payable' (its vest pass does not filter on delivery). consume_fee_credit then skips it forever because of `delivery = 'credit'`. Separately, an operator who flips bonus_cash_payout_enabled to true gets no behaviour change whatsoever, because nothing reads it.
money_impact: Charged and never delivered — the exact failure class the 20260806240000 and 20260806320000 migrations were written to eliminate for poster discounts, still live on the bonus rail. Every such bonus consumes bonus_cents of budget and one of max_redemptions while the referrer receives nothing and sees nothing (there is no client surface for bonus_ledger at all — grep of src/ and web/ returns zero references). The second harm is a false sense of safety: the flag is cited in CLAUDE.md and in the migration header as the gate on the cash rail, so whoever builds cash payout will reasonably assume the gate already exists and is being enforced.
evidence: Flag defined and never read — supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:223-228 `insert into public.app_flags (key, enabled, note) values ('bonus_cash_payout_enabled', false, 'OFF. Bonuses accrue as fee CREDITS only...')`; the only other occurrence in the whole tree is the comment at 20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:23. The real (and only) gate — 20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:183 `where user_id = p_user and state = 'payable' and delivery = 'credit'`. The minting path propagates the promotion's delivery verbatim — 20260806250000_referral_once_per_person.sql:74 `values (referrer, promo.id, 'referral', promo.bonus_cents, promo.bonus_delivery, 'pending', ...)`. Column allows it — 20260806070000_promotions.sql:62-63 `bonus_delivery text not null default 'credit' check (bonus_delivery in ('credit','cash'))`.
fix_sketch: Either refuse to mint when `promo.bonus_delivery = 'cash' and not app_flags.bonus_cash_payout_enabled` (fail closed, no charge), or force delivery to 'credit' at mint time while the flag is off. Add a control: any bonus_ledger row with delivery='cash' in state 'payable' for more than N hours is undeliverable value charged to a campaign.
verifier_note: Downgraded medium -> low because today it fails in the SAFE direction and no reachable path creates the bad state. admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts createPromotion (lines 23-79) never sets bonus_delivery, so every console-created bonus promotion takes the 'credit' default; clonePromotion (line 203-232) spreads ...rest and would copy 'cash', but only from a source row that itself cannot be created through the console. Producing a delivery='cash' promotion requires a direct service-role or SQL-editor insert — an operator action, not an attacker path. And flipping the flag to true produces no behaviour change, which is fail-safe rather than fail-open. So the real defect is documentation-shaped: a flag cited in CLAUDE.md and in a migration header as the gate on the cash rail, which is not wired to anything, so whoever builds cash payout will assume an enforcement point that does not exist. Worth fixing; not a live money exposure.

title: vest_bonuses' reversal check misses every reversal that does not go through the admin console, and one of its two conditions is structurally dead
summary: The void condition is `coalesce(p.refunded_cents,0) > 0 or p.status = 'refunded'`. The second disjunct can never be true: payments.status carries a CHECK constraining it to ('authorized','captured','cancelled','failed'), and 20260804010000 states refusing a 'refunded' status was deliberate. The first disjunct is written only by record_refund, i.e. only by admin-console refunds — so a refund issued from the Stripe Dashboard, or a lost chargeback, never voids a pending bonus.
trigger: The pair mints a bonus, then the poster disputes the charge with their card issuer. stripe-webhook's charge.refunded / charge.dispute.created handlers insert a disputes row and email an admin but never touch payments.refunded_cents (this is the repo's own documented defect — ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered, 20260806040000_control_library.sql:649). Result: refunded_cents stays 0 and p.status stays 'captured', so vest_bonuses' void pass never matches. The dispute row does block the vest pass while status is 'open'/'investigating' — but the moment an operator resolves or rejects it, the bonus vests, and per finding #1 nothing can reverse it thereafter.
money_impact: The advertised protection "a bonus is voided if the source booking was reversed" holds only for the console refund path. Reversals the platform did not initiate — which are precisely the ones a farmer would engineer, since they cost the farmer nothing and require no operator cooperation — pass straight through. Loss = bonus_cents per event, on top of the money already lost to the reversal itself.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:138-141 `select 1 from public.payments p where p.booking_id = b.source_booking_id and (coalesce(p.refunded_cents, 0) > 0 or p.status = 'refunded')`. The status value cannot exist — supabase/migration_stripe.sql:30-31 `status text not null default 'authorized' check (status in ('authorized','captured','cancelled','failed'))`, and 20260804010000_phase1_admin_ops.sql explicitly says "Deliberately NOT a new status value". refunded_cents has exactly one writer — 20260804020000_refund_ledger_fixes.sql:110 inside record_refund, which is `grant execute ... to service_role` only and is called from the admin console path.
fix_sketch: Void on the same signals the dispute/chargeback webhook already produces: add `or exists (select 1 from public.disputes d where d.booking_id = b.source_booking_id and d.reversal_cents is not null)` and drop the dead `p.status = 'refunded'` disjunct so the condition stops reading as if it covered more than it does.
verifier_note: The headline claim — 'a refund from the Stripe Dashboard, or a lost chargeback, never voids a pending bonus' — is materially overstated and must be corrected. Both charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created call recordReversal (stripe-webhook/index.ts:292 and :318), which inserts a disputes row with status defaulting to 'open' (20260804010000:83). vest_bonuses' vest pass explicitly refuses to vest while any dispute on the source booking is open or investigating (20260806080000:147-150). So an externally-initiated reversal DOES hold the bonus at 'pending' — and if an operator subsequently records the reversal, refunded_cents becomes non-zero and the void pass (which runs first, line 133) catches it on the next sweep. The genuine residual is narrower: a reversal whose disputes row an operator resolves or rejects WITHOUT ever pressing 'Record chargeback', so refunded_cents stays 0 and the bonus then vests. That is precisely the known ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered defect (20260806040000:649), and the new consequence — that it silently converts an unreversed ledger into a paid-out referral bonus — is not named in that control's rationale. Loss is one bonus_cents of margin per such event, downstream of a much larger loss the platform already took. Severity low.

title: Referral farming is bounded but profitable at roughly 10:1 on fee cost, and mutual + retroactive referrals halve the cost again
summary: The vest-on-outcome design does defeat the pure non-working farmer — a fee credit has zero or negative cash-out value to someone who does no real work, because burning it requires being the earner on a booking that still costs at least the Stripe processing floor. But for a farmer who is ALSO a real worker the credit is worth face value, and the cost of minting one is the platform fee on a single $10 gig. Two structural gaps make it cheaper still: referrals rows can be inserted by the referred user at any time (no signup-window constraint), and there is nothing forbidding A-refers-B and B-refers-A simultaneously, so one colluding pair yields two bonuses.
trigger: Farmer controls account A (a genuine worker) plus N sock accounts B_i, each with Stripe Connect onboarding completed. For each i: A posts a $10 gig, B_i books it, both mark done, A verifies (capture succeeds — this is enforced: 20260625040000:76-78 requires a captured payments row before completed->verified). accrue_referral_bonus mints bonus_cents to A. Seven days later the sweep vests it. A spends the credits against the platform fee on gigs A was going to work anyway. Additionally, because referrals is keyed only on referred_id, A can also insert a row saying B_i referred A — B_i then collects a second bonus on A's next verified gig. And because accrue_referral_bonus never compares referrals.created_at to the booking, the referral row can be inserted the minute before a gig verifies.
money_impact: ARITHMETIC. Minimum gig is $10 (guard_job_pay_floor: `new.pay < 10`). platform_fee_cents(1000c, 1000bps) = max(round-half-up(100), ceil(1000*0.029)+30+25 = 84) = 100c. So one referral cycle costs the pair exactly $1.00 of real cash (the poster's card is charged $10, the earner nets $9.00; the platform pays Stripe ~$0.59 out of that $1.00). Yield: bonus_cents as a fee credit. Realizing it needs headroom = 0.071*M - 55 cents per gig of M cents; a $10 credit is fully absorbed by one $149 gig, or spread across several. On the console's own defaults (budget $250, max_redemptions 100) a $10-bonus campaign funds 25 bonuses, so ONE farmer with 25 sock earner accounts spends 25 x $1.00 = $25 in platform fees to capture 100% of the $250 budget — a 10:1 return — realized at face value against fees they would have paid on roughly $3,700 of genuine earning work. With mutual referrals the same 25 sock accounts yield 50 bonuses (bonus_ledger_one_per_referral is on (user_id, source_user_id), so (A,B) and (B,A) are distinct rows), i.e. $12.50 of fees to exhaust the budget. VERDICT: loss IS bounded by budget_cents, so this is not an unbounded rail; but the migration header's claim that farming "stops being PROFITABLE" is false — it is unprofitable only for someone who never works, and the real remaining friction is Stripe Connect Express onboarding per sock account (stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:118 requires stripe_accounts.onboarded for the earner), which is enforced by Stripe, not by this codebase.
evidence: Referral can be attached at any time by the referred user, with no signup-window or ordering constraint — supabase/migration_referrals.sql:12 `create policy "referrals_insert_self" on public.referrals for insert with check (auth.uid() = referred_id);` and the consumer does no timestamp comparison: 20260806250000_referral_once_per_person.sql:56-57 `select r.referrer_id into referrer from public.referrals r where r.referred_id = new.earner_id;` — the only rejection is self-referral (line 58). Mutual referrals are unconstrained: the table's only key is `referred_id uuid primary key` (migration_referrals.sql:6). Per-pair guard is on the ordered pair — 20260806250000:38 `on public.bonus_ledger (user_id, source_user_id)`. Min pay — 20260728120000_min_job_pay_floor.sql:41 `if new.pay is null or new.pay < 10 then`. Fee floor — 20260806140000_fee_overflow_fix.sql:49-50.
fix_sketch: Require the referrals row to predate the source booking (`r.created_at < new.created_at`) so a referral cannot be attached retroactively to work already in flight. Reject reciprocal pairs (`not exists (select 1 from referrals where referred_id = referrer and referrer_id = new.earner_id)`). Consider requiring the referred person's qualifying gig to be with a counterparty who is neither the referrer nor a prior counterparty of the referrer, and to clear a minimum value well above the $10 floor — the $1 mint cost is what makes the 10:1 arithmetic work.
verifier_note: The 'mutual referrals yield 50 bonuses for $12.50' arithmetic is REFUTED and must be struck. public.referrals declares `referred_id uuid primary key` (supabase/migration_referrals.sql:6), so any given account can be the REFERRED party in at most one row for its entire lifetime. A can therefore be referred by exactly one B_i, not by all 25. Mutual pairing yields 26 bonuses, not 50 — and the extra one lands on B_1's ledger, where it is nearly worthless: B_1's gigs are the $10 shams, whose headroom is 0.071*1000 - 55 = 16c each. Cost per bonus stays at $1.00, not $0.50. The 'retroactive attach' point is also weaker than presented: the RLS policy is `with check (auth.uid() = referred_id)` (migration_referrals.sql:12), so only the referred person can create the row — a farmer cannot retro-attach themselves as referrer to a stranger who is about to have a gig verified, only to accounts they already control, where the timing was never a constraint anyway. Downgraded to low overall: the loss is bounded by budget_cents (the finding concedes this), the attack needs N Stripe Connect Express accounts each cleared through Stripe KYC (stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:118 requires stripe_accounts.onboarded), and it needs thousands of dollars of genuine work to realise the credits. The durable takeaway is that the header comment overclaims, and that a $10 pay floor is what makes the mint cost trivially small — raise the qualifying-gig threshold, not the guardrails.

title: A broken vesting job can never page — vest_bonuses is not a registered control, its failures are swallowed as warnings, and its only detector is a medium-severity finding that the pager filters out
summary: vest_bonuses() runs inside controls_sweep_and_page wrapped in `exception when others then raise warning`, so a failure leaves no row in controls, no last_error, and no finding. The single detector, ctl_bonus_vesting_stalled, is registered at severity 'medium' and only reports rows 2 days past vests_at. controls-alert's page mode filters fresh findings to `['critical','high']`, so it never pages; the failure surfaces only in the once-a-day digest body, at least 9 days after the first affected bonus was earned.
trigger: vest_bonuses starts raising (a schema change to payments or disputes, a permissions change, a lock timeout). Every hourly sweep prints a warning to the Postgres log and proceeds. run_all_controls reports 0 errored and 0 stale because vest_bonuses is not in the controls registry. Users who earned referral bonuses are silently not paid. Nine days later a medium finding appears — visible only if someone reads the daily digest email past the critical/high section.
money_impact: No direct loss to the platform; the loss is to users who earned a bonus and are silently not credited, plus loss of truth about the money system. The repo's own doctrine ("a control that errors or goes stale is reported as loudly as a violation") is not satisfied for this job, because the job is not a control. Note the mitigations that DO exist and were verified: the pg_cron entries are created idempotently (20260806030000:107-109), the final controls_sweep_and_page still calls vest_bonuses first (20260806330000:31-35), CREATE OR REPLACE preserves the service_role grant, and the separate controls_digest cron reports stale controls daily — so a wholesale sweep outage would be caught. It is specifically vesting failing while the sweep succeeds that is invisible.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806330000_dispatch_timeouts.sql:30-35 `begin perform public.vest_bonuses(); exception when others then raise warning 'bonus vesting failed: %', sqlerrm; end;` — no finding, no controls row updated. Detector severity — 20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:322 registers ctl_bonus_vesting_stalled as `'medium', 'money'`, and its predicate is `b.state = 'pending' and b.vests_at < now() - interval '2 days'` (line 316-317). Pager filter — supabase/functions/controls-alert/index.ts:115-117 `const fresh = open.filter((f) => ['critical','high'].includes(f.severity) && Date.parse(f.first_seen_at) >= cutoff);` and :119 `if (mode === 'page' && fresh.length === 0 && errored.length === 0 && stale.length === 0) return json({ ok: true, emailed: false, reason: 'nothing_new' });`
fix_sketch: Register vesting as a control in its own right (e.g. ctl_vesting_last_run, high severity) writing last_run_at/last_error from the sweep's exception handler, so a vesting failure lands in `errored` — which page mode DOES alert on regardless of severity. Alternatively raise ctl_bonus_vesting_stalled to 'high' and shorten its 2-day grace to a few hours, since the sweep is hourly.
verifier_note: Confirmed as written, with credit for the mitigations the finding already verified. Kept at low: no platform loss, no attacker path, and the failure is self-limiting in the sense that the rows stay 'pending' rather than being lost. The harm is a delayed, under-alerted debt to users who earned a credit. The suggested fix is the right shape — the cheapest version is to raise ctl_bonus_vesting_stalled to 'high' and cut its 2-day grace to a few hours given the sweep is hourly, since the pager already alerts on high regardless of the errored/stale channels.

title: A fee credit is burned in full at booking but delivered only pro-rata at a partial capture; up to 50% of an earned credit evaporates with nothing settling it back
summary: consume_fee_credit flips bonus_ledger rows to state='applied' for the FULL headroom computed against the quoted amount at INSERT. stripe-capture-payment then scales the credited fee by capturePct on a partial capture, so the delivered relief is credit*pct while the ledger was charged credit*1. settle_booking_benefits — the one function whose entire job is 'settle the reserve to what actually happened at capture' — iterates only promo_redemptions and never touches bonus_ledger, so the unspent portion is neither returned to the user nor recorded anywhere.
trigger: Earner has a $10 referral credit (state='payable'). They book a $100 gig at the standing 1000 bps. pin_booking_amount → consume_fee_credit takes headroom = platform_fee_cents(10000,1000) - (ceil(10000*0.029)+30+25) = 1000 - 345 = 655c, marks that portion 'applied', leaves 345c on the ledger. Poster later uses CompletionModal 'report a problem' and pays 50%. stripe-capture-payment takes the partial branch.
money_impact:
Verified arithmetic across the matrix (capturePctFinal is clamped to [0.5,1] at stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:71, so the worst case is exactly half):
  $100 gig @1000bps: headroom/charged = 655c. At pct=1.00 delivered 655c (lost 0). At pct=0.75 delivered 491c (lost 164c). At pct=0.50 delivered 327c (LOST 328c).
  $500 gig @1000bps: charged 3495c; at pct=0.50 delivered 1747c, LOST 1748c.
  $100 gig @3000bps: charged 2655c; at pct=0.50 delivered 1327c, LOST 1328c.
The loser is the referrer — a user who earned this by referring a real person who completed a real gig and paid real fees on both sides. The platform quietly keeps the difference as extra margin on the disputed booking. Cross-check: at bps 0 headroom is 0 and nothing is consumed (correct), and at pct=1 delivery is exact (correct) — the defect is confined to the partial path, which is precisely the path a poster can trigger unilaterally.
No control sees it: ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking (20260806260000:105) requires bk.status in ('declined','cancelled') AND no capture; this booking is 'verified' and captured. ctl_benefit_never_settled reads promo_redemptions only. __tests__/pricing.test.js has zero references to platform_fee_after_credit, headroom, or credits (grep returns nothing), so the drift test does not cover this either.
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:169 — settle_booking_benefits' only loop:
  `for r in select * from public.promo_redemptions where booking_id = p_booking and released_at is null and settled_at is null for update loop` … the body updates only public.promotions and public.promo_redemptions. `bonus_ledger` appears nowhere in the function.

supabase/functions/stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:179 — the partial branch:
  `const feeCents = Math.min(captureCents, Math.round(fullFeeCents * capturePct));`
where fullFeeCents = fullFeeForAuth = platform_fee_after_credit(gigAmount, bps, creditCents) (index.ts:150-163). Scaling the ALREADY-credited fee by pct scales the credit's value by pct too.

supabase/migrations/20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:176 — the charge is sized against the FULL quoted amount, once, at INSERT:
  `headroom := greatest(0, public.platform_fee_cents(p_amount_cents, p_fee_bps) - (ceil(coalesce(p_amount_cents,0)*0.029)::integer + 30 + 25));`
fix_sketch: Extend settle_booking_benefits (or add a sibling called from the same site in stripe-capture-payment) to recompute the usable headroom at p_amount_cents and return the difference to bonus_ledger — mirroring consume_fee_credit's split: insert a fresh state='payable' row for (charged - delivered) owned by the same user, leaving the 'applied' row as the audit record of what was actually used. Then widen ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking (or add a new control) to assert bookings.fee_credit_cents delivered == sum of bonus_ledger applied against that booking, for captured bookings too.
verifier_note: Two mechanical corrections. (1) The finding's fix sketch is right that settle_booking_benefits is the natural site, but note the delivered relief on a partial is not merely `credit*pct` — it is `round(fee(A)*pct) - round(max(floor(A), fee(A)-credit)*pct)`, so a correct settle must recompute usable headroom at the CAPTURED amount (fee(capturedGig) - floor(capturedGig)), not scale the pinned number. On the worked $100/50% case that correct figure is 500-200=300c, meaning the ledger should get back 355c, not 328c. (2) A NEW consequence the finding misses and that the code's own comments do not name: the partial branch violates the design's stated absolute Stripe-processing floor. At pct=0.5 the platform collects a 173c application fee on a 5000c capture whose floor is ceil(5000*0.029)+30+25=200c, so the platform pays 27c of Stripe processing out of pocket — the exact thing consume_fee_credit's comment says 'we never' do. Algebraically the shortfall is 55*(1-pct), i.e. up to ~27c per partially-captured booking that carries a credit. Small, but it is the same scaling bug pointing the other way and it invalidates the 'loss ceiling is structural' claim in 20260806080000's header.

title: A fee credit spent on a booking that is later refunded or charged back is lost permanently — release refuses because the payment was captured, and nothing else restores it
summary: release_booking_benefits is the only function in the repo that ever moves a bonus_ledger row from 'applied' back to 'payable', and it early-returns 0 whenever a payment for the booking is captured. A refund or a lost chargeback fully reverses the money — admin-payment-action passes refund_application_fee: true, so the platform hands back the very fee the credit discounted — but the credit stays 'applied' forever. vest_bonuses explicitly voids a PENDING bonus when its SOURCE booking is reversed, proving the system tracks reversals; there is no equivalent on the SPEND side.
trigger: Referrer holds a vested 655c credit. They book and complete a $100 gig; capture succeeds (fee 345c after credit). Trust/finance later issues a full refund from /payments (op='refund'), or the poster wins a chargeback and an operator files op='record_reversal'. payments.status becomes 'refunded'/captured_at stays set; record_refund debits the earner's in-app earnings back down. The transaction is fully unwound — except the credit.
money_impact: The earner loses the entire consumed portion of the credit (655c on the worked example, up to 3495c on a $500 gig) for a booking whose money was 100% reversed. They received exactly nothing for it: the fee it offset was itself refunded to the poster. This is the identical harm 20260806260000's own header calls 'value silently taken from a user for work that never happened' — that migration fixed decline/cancel and left refund/chargeback uncovered. Nothing detects it: ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking (:105) filters `bk.status in ('declined','cancelled') and not exists (captured payment)`, and a refunded booking fails both halves. ctl_external_reversal_not_ledgered and ctl_payment_ledger_impossible never read bonus_ledger.
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260806260000_release_fee_credits.sql:44-51 —
  `select exists (select 1 from public.payments pay where pay.booking_id = p_booking and (pay.status = 'captured' or pay.captured_at is not null)) into captured;`
  `if captured then return 0; end if;`
The bonus_ledger restore at :78 (`update public.bonus_ledger set state='payable', applied_at=null, applied_booking_id=null where applied_booking_id = p_booking and state='applied'`) is BELOW that early return and is therefore unreachable for any captured booking.

supabase/functions/admin-payment-action/index.ts:187 — `refund_application_fee: true` (the platform's fee is returned with the refund).

supabase/migrations/20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:131-138 — vest_bonuses voids only state='pending' rows: `update public.bonus_ledger b set state='void' … where b.state = 'pending' and exists (select 1 from public.payments p where p.booking_id = b.source_booking_id and (coalesce(p.refunded_cents,0) > 0 or p.status='refunded'))`. Note it keys on source_booking_id (where the bonus was EARNED), never applied_booking_id (where it was SPENT).

Grep confirms no other writer: `bonus_ledger` is written only in 20260806070000 (DDL), 20260806080000 (vest/consume), 20260806250000 (accrue), 20260806260000 (release). No edge function and no admin action writes it.
fix_sketch: Split the captured guard: keep refusing to claw back the promo campaign's reserve on a captured booking, but restore the fee credit in proportion to the reversal. Simplest correct form: in the refund path (record_refund, or a new trigger on payments.refunded_cents) return round(fee_credit_delivered * refunded_cents / captured_total) to bonus_ledger as a fresh 'payable' row. Add a control asserting no bonus_ledger row is 'applied' against a booking whose payment is fully refunded/reversed.
verifier_note: One factual error in the trigger narrative that should not be repeated in a report: 'payments.status becomes refunded' is FALSE. Nothing in the repo ever writes payments.status='refunded' — grep for that literal returns exactly one hit, and it is a READ inside vest_bonuses (20260806080000:140), not a write. record_refund sets only refunded_cents/refunded_at, leaving status='captured'. The conclusion is unchanged (the early return also tests captured_at, which is set), but the mechanism is 'status stays captured', not 'status flips to refunded'. Worth noting as a side effect: because no writer ever sets that status, the `or p.status='refunded'` half of vest_bonuses' void predicate is dead code — the `refunded_cents > 0` half is what actually does the work there, and it does work, so the void-on-reversal path for PENDING bonuses is intact. That asymmetry (source-side reversal handled, spend-side reversal not) is exactly the finding's point and it holds.

title: promotions_enabled — the documented 'everything off at once' incident switch — does not reach referral-bonus accrual or fee-credit spending, and bonus_ledger has no per-user revoke
summary: Three of the four benefit consumers check app_flags.promotions_enabled (consume_promo_grant, consume_poster_discount, redeem_promo_code). consume_fee_credit checks nothing at all — no kill switch, no promotion status, no ends_at, no expiry on the ledger row. The final accrue_referral_bonus (20260806250000:41) also omits the flag. So flipping the master switch OFF during an incident stops fee overrides, poster discounts and code redemption while referral bonuses keep minting against the campaign budget and existing credits keep being applied to new bookings — directly contradicting the flag's own note.
trigger: Ops discovers referral farming in progress and flips app_flags.promotions_enabled = false from /flags (the one lever the design documents for 'this is being abused'). New bookings by any earner holding a payable credit continue to consume it at INSERT; every gig a referred earner verifies continues to mint a new bonus row and increment promotions.spent_cents/redemptions_used. Pausing the campaign (status='paused') stops accrual — but not spending, because consume_fee_credit never looks at the promotion at all, only at bonus_ledger.state='payable'.
money_impact: Bounded but not stoppable. Accrual exposure stays capped by budget_cents/max_redemptions (the increment-is-the-check UPDATE at 20260806250000:88 is intact), so the incident cannot exceed the campaign budget — but the operator cannot halt it below that ceiling with the tool built for exactly that purpose. Spend-side exposure is every already-payable credit in the ledger, uncapped by any flag and with no expiry: bonus_ledger has no revoked_at, no expires_at, and the console's revokeGrant (admin/app/(console)/promotions/actions.ts:234) updates promo_grants only. vest_bonuses can only void state='pending' rows, so once a credit is payable there is NO code path in the repo that can take it back — remediation requires hand-written service-role SQL, which is the exact failure /promotions and /flags were built to eliminate. Secondary consequence: a paused or ended 'bonus' campaign keeps having its budget drawn down by consume_fee_credit's beneficiaries without any live campaign behind the spend.
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260806080000_referral_bonus.sql:160-172 — consume_fee_credit's entire preamble:
  `begin
     if p_user is null then return 0; end if;
     headroom := greatest(0, ...);`
No app_flags read, no join to promotions, no state/expiry check beyond `state='payable' and delivery='credit'`.

Contrast supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:245 (consume_promo_grant) and 20260806340000_discount_kind_confusion.sql:72 (consume_poster_discount), both of which open with:
  `if not coalesce((select enabled from public.app_flags where key = 'promotions_enabled'), true) then return null/0; end if;`

supabase/migrations/20260806250000_referral_once_per_person.sql:41-66 — accrue_referral_bonus checks `kind='bonus' and status='active' and starts_at <= now() and (ends_at is null or ends_at > now())` but never promotions_enabled.

The claim being violated, supabase/migrations/20260806070000_promotions.sql:23-24 and :214-217:
  `--   3. app_flags.promotions_enabled = false → everything off at once. Incident switch.`
  `'Master switch for ALL promotions. OFF = no code redeems and no grant applies to a NEW booking.'`
fix_sketch: Add the same promotions_enabled guard to the head of consume_fee_credit and accrue_referral_bonus. Separately, give bonus_ledger a revoked_at/void-by-admin path (an admin action that flips payable→void with a reason and an audit row) so abuse discovered after vesting has a lever short of raw SQL, and add a control asserting the four benefit consumers all honour the flag.
verifier_note: One sub-claim is REFUTED outright and must be dropped: 'a paused or ended bonus campaign keeps having its budget drawn down by consume_fee_credit's beneficiaries'. consume_fee_credit does not write public.promotions at all — I read the entire body; it only UPDATEs bonus_ledger rows. The campaign budget is charged ONCE, at accrual (20260806250000:87), against promo.bonus_cents. Spending a credit later moves no campaign money, so pausing or ending the campaign cannot leak budget through the spend path and there is no 'spend with no live campaign behind it' accounting hole. The accurate residual finding is narrower: the master incident switch does not cover referral-bonus accrual (per-campaign pause does), and a vested payable credit has no admin void path short of service-role SQL. Both are ops-lever gaps, not loss vectors.

title: A credit consumed by an application the poster never answers is frozen indefinitely, and the control that would catch it only looks at declined/cancelled bookings
summary: consume_fee_credit runs at booking INSERT — i.e. the moment the earner APPLIES, long before anyone agrees to anything. Release is driven exclusively by trg_zz_release_benefits, which fires only when status transitions into 'declined' or 'cancelled'. Nothing in the repo expires a pending booking, so a poster who simply ignores an application leaves the earner's credit in state='applied' forever, and ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking cannot report it because the booking's status is still 'pending'.
trigger: Earner with a payable credit applies to a gig. The poster never taps accept or decline (ctl_stranded_pending_booking's own registration text says this is common enough to expect a large initial count). The booking sits 'pending'; the credit sits 'applied' against it. The earner's next application gets no credit, because the ledger shows nothing payable.
money_impact: The full consumed headroom (655c on a $100 gig at the standing rate) is unavailable to the earner for an unbounded period, and the earner has no way to reclaim it: the guard only lets the earner move pending→cancelled, so their only recovery is to cancel their own application — which they have no reason to know they must do, because no screen ever shows them they hold a credit or that one was spent (see the disclosure finding). The one control that names credits filters them out by status; ctl_stranded_pending_booking exists but is registered under domain 'lifecycle' at severity 'medium' and its detail payload says nothing about a locked credit, so an operator working that queue frees the slot and never returns the money.
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260806260000_release_fee_credits.sql:105-124 — ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking:
  `where b.state = 'applied' and bk.status in ('declined', 'cancelled') and not exists (select 1 from public.payments p where p.booking_id = bk.id and (p.status='captured' or p.captured_at is not null))`
'pending' is absent from that IN list.

supabase/migrations/20260806220000_benefit_lifecycle.sql:207-213 — the only release trigger:
  `if new.status in ('declined','cancelled') and coalesce(old.status,'') is distinct from new.status then perform public.release_booking_benefits(new.id, 'booking_' || new.status); end if;`
  `create trigger trg_zz_release_benefits after update of status on public.bookings ...`

supabase/migrations/20260806040000_control_library.sql:665 — ctl_stranded_pending_booking's own registration: 'nothing in the system ever expires one'.
fix_sketch: Either move credit consumption from booking INSERT to hold placement (stripe-create-payment-intent, where the poster has actually accepted), or add 'pending' to ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking with an age threshold matching ctl_stranded_pending_booking's, and have the sweep call release_booking_benefits for pending bookings past that age.
verifier_note: The claim 'the earner has no way to reclaim it' and 'an operator working that queue frees the slot and never returns the money' are both wrong. Cancelling the pending booking — which the earner can do themselves and which is exactly what an operator does to remediate ctl_stranded_pending_booking — fires trg_zz_release_benefits and restores the bonus_ledger rows to 'payable', because there is no captured payment on a pending booking so release_booking_benefits' early return does not bind. The accurate residual is: (a) ctl_credit_stranded_on_dead_booking's status filter does not cover 'pending', so a locked credit on an aged application is invisible to the credit-specific control; and (b) the earner is never told a credit was spent, so they have no reason to know cancelling would free it. Both are disclosure/coverage, not value destruction.

title: The earner never sees a credit before it is spent, and the receipt line reports the pinned amount rather than the amount actually delivered
summary: There is no surface anywhere in the mobile or web app that shows an earner their bonus_ledger balance — the only grep hits for credits/bonuses in src/ and web/ are unrelated. The credit is consumed silently inside a DB trigger at application time. The single place it is ever disclosed is the payment receipt, which renders payments.fee_credit_cents (the pin) as a positive line item; after a partial capture that number overstates the relief actually received by up to 2x, and it does not reconcile against the other lines on the same sheet.
trigger: Open Payments → tap a settled gig that was captured at 50%. The DetailSheet renders 'Gig total $100.00 / Platform fee (10%) − $1.73 / Fee credit applied + $6.55' against a net of $48.27. The credit line says $6.55; the relief actually delivered was $3.27 (see the partial-capture finding).
money_impact: Disclosure, not direct loss, but it is the reason the two loss findings above are invisible to the people they cost. An earner cannot notice that half their credit vanished, because the receipt asserts the full amount was applied; and they cannot notice a credit was frozen on an ignored application, because no screen ever told them they had one. Also note 'Gig total' is payments.amount_cents, the full AUTHORIZED hold, which stripe-capture-payment deliberately never rewrites on a partial capture (index.ts:186-188) — so on any partial the receipt's line items sum to $104.82 against a stated net of $48.27.
evidence:
src/screens/PaymentsScreen.js:417 —
  `entry.feeCreditCents > 0 && { label: 'Fee credit applied', value: `+ ${fmt(entry.feeCreditCents)}`, good: true },`
src/lib/payments.js:101 — `feeCreditCents: cents(row.fee_credit_cents)` sourced from the payments row, which pin_payment_fee_bps copies verbatim from bookings.fee_credit_cents at INSERT and freezes on UPDATE (20260806110000_poster_discounts.sql:229-252). The pin is never adjusted by the partial-capture branch, which rewrites only fee_cents and earner_amount_cents.
src/lib/payments.js:73 — `const gross = cents(row.amount_cents);` (the authorized total, not the captured one).
Grep for a pre-booking credit surface across src/screens, src/lib, src/components, web/app, web/lib returns no bonus_ledger or credit-balance reads.
fix_sketch: Store the DELIVERED credit alongside the pinned one (e.g. payments.fee_credit_applied_cents, written in the same UPDATE that sets fee_cents) and render that on the receipt; derive 'Gig total' from earner_amount_cents + fee_cents on a captured row so the sheet reconciles. Add a credit balance row to the earnings dashboard reading bonus_ledger where state='payable' (the owner-scoped RLS policy bonus_ledger_own_select already permits it).
verifier_note: Sharpen the primary defect: the independent, credit-agnostic bug is that on any partial capture the earner receipt shows payments.amount_cents (the authorized hold) as 'Gig total' while the payout total is derived from the reduced earner_amount_cents, so the sheet's line items never sum to its own total — no credit required to reproduce. The 'Fee credit applied' overstatement is a consequence of finding 1, not a separate defect, and would be fixed by either recording the delivered credit or correcting the delivery itself. Also note the finding's own suggested fix leans on bonus_ledger_own_select — I confirmed that policy exists (20260806070000:209-211, `for select using (auth.uid() = user_id)`), so an owner-scoped balance read is in fact already permitted by RLS and needs no policy work.

title: settle_booking_benefits is kind-blind: every poster-discount charge is refunded to the campaign at capture, so budget_cents stops bounding the loss
summary: settle_booking_benefits() runs at capture over EVERY unreleased redemption on the booking and re-prices it with promo_benefit_cents(amount, r.fee_bps) — a fee_override formula. A poster_discount redemption stores r.fee_bps = the booking's fee_bps_quoted, which is normally the standing rate, so promo_benefit_cents returns 0, delta = -reserved_cents, and the campaign's spent_cents is decremented back by the exact amount of the discount that was actually delivered. The money left the platform; the budget line item did not.
trigger: Any booking that consumed a poster discount and is then captured (stripe-capture-payment/index.ts:241 calls settle_booking_benefits on every capture). No promo/tier needed; the plain case is the standing rate with no earner benefit.
money_impact: Worked example, $100 gig at the standing 1000 bps: platform_fee_cents = 1000, floor = ceil(0.029*10000)+30+25 = 345, headroom = 655. Campaign '$5 off your first hire': poster_discount_cents = 500, budget_cents = 25000 ($250), max_redemptions = 100 (console default, and editPromotion/createPromotion impose NO upper bound and no relation to budget). consume_poster_discount charges hit = 500, spent_cents 0 -> 500; the poster is charged 9500 and application_fee_amount is 500 instead of 1000, so the platform really loses $5. At capture, settle computes actual = least(15000, promo_benefit_cents(10000, 1000)) = least(15000, 1000-1000) = 0, delta = -500, spent_cents 500 -> 0. redemptions_used is NOT decremented (only release_booking_benefits does that), so the sole surviving bound is max_redemptions. Intended maximum loss = min($250 budget, 100 x $5) = $250 (50 discounts). Actual loss = 100 x $5 = $500 — 2x the budget; at max_redemptions = 1000 with the same $250 budget it is $5,000, 20x. Throughout, /promotions shows spent_cents oscillating 0 -> 500 -> 0, i.e. a burn-down bar that reads ~0% while the campaign is spending.
